messages:
Anna (ML Eng): Quick question — we're finalizing how to ship quant profiles for Redwood Optimize. What's the minimal manifest we should require and what's the canonical naming/versioning scheme? Need this for the CLI + docs.
Ravi (Optimize): Keep it tiny and audit-friendly. Manifest should include model, quant_scheme, profile_id, version, accuracy_delta, perf_metrics, eval_ref (hash or id), and recommended_routes/fallbacks. Naming: <model>-<quant>-<profile>-<semver>. Example: llama3-13b-awq-latency-1.0.0. :white_check_mark:
Lucas (Eval): +1. Also include eval_seedset and prompt_set_hash so we can trace regressions back to exact prompts. Keep accuracy_delta as signed percentage relative to fp32 baseline.
Anna (ML Eng): Nice. Can we show a micro example of manifest JSON so docs writers have something concrete?
Ravi (Optimize): Sure — something like:```json
{
  "model": "llama3-13b",
  "quant_scheme": "AWQ-4bit",
  "profile_id": "latency",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "accuracy_delta": "-0.8%",
  "perf_metrics": { "tokens_per_sec": "2400", "p95_latency_ms": "120" },
  "eval_ref": "eval-2026-02-18-rc3",
  "prompt_set_hash": "sha256:abcd1234...",
  "recommended_routes": ["dedicated-us-west-2:llama3-13b-awq-latency-1.0.0"],
  "fallback_models": ["llama3-13b-int8-1.0.0"]
}
```
Lucas (Eval): Make sure perf metrics are normalized to tokens/sec per GPU and that we record batch size + sequence length used. Otherwise numbers are misleading.
Sarah (Product): For the naming scheme, can we reserve a slot for 'intent' (e.g., latency, cost, quality)? That helps the console show recommended profile types.
Ravi (Optimize): Yes — profile_id covers intent. Enforce ascii lowercase + hyphens only. Versioning: semver where major bumps indicate a quality/regression-impacting change (e.g., different prompt set or quant algorithm), minor for perf tweaks, patch for metadata fixes.
Anna (ML Eng): How do we package artifacts? .qpkg tar with manifest.json at root + binary artifacts under /blobs. CLI should verify manifest signature/hash.
quant-bot: Auto-scan finished: 3 candidate profiles found for llama3-13b AWQ. See /optimize/candidates/llama3-13b-awq-20260318 :robot_face:
Ravi (Optimize): Also include an optional field optimize_recs as an array of strings for quick ingestion by Optimize UI, e.g., ["batch_per_gpu:8", "kv_cache:true", "prefill_threads:2"]. Keep this stable across versions.
Lucas (Eval): Add 'compatibilities' list to indicate supported runtimes (runtime-v1, runtime-v2-gpu, onprem-hw-X). Helps routing.
Ravi (Optimize): Good call. CLI validation rules: 1) model normalized, 2) quant_scheme in canonical set (AWQ, GPTQ, INT8, FP8), 3) accuracy_delta present, 4) perf metrics contain tokens_per_sec and p95_latency_ms. Failing validation returns non-zero + UX-friendly errors.
Anna (ML Eng): Edge cases: if accuracy_delta > -1.5% mark as 'requires_review' and don't auto-promote. Add status field: draft/validated/released/retired.
Sarah (Product): We'll reflect status in Console and Optimize recommendations. UI will surface 'recommended for' based on profile_id and accuracy thresholds.
Ravi (Optimize): Implementation note — when we re-run evals with new prompt sets, create new version and link old one via 'supersedes' field. That keeps history.
Anna (ML Eng): Perfect. Action items: I'll draft the schema PR and sample CLI output. Ravi will write validation tests and publish canonical set of quant_scheme strings. Lucas will attach recommended eval seedset and prompt hash process. :thumbsup:
Ravi (Optimize): I'll aim to have the validator prototype by EOD.
Anna (ML Eng): Thanks — this gives docs + product exactly what we need.
